blocks.text: The unit of analysis is a static theoretical model in which the equilibrium axioms of the dense-matter equation of state are relaxed to include rotational and thermal support from binary accretion. The protocol specifies three independent axes: the binary accretion parameters, the causality bound, and the equilibrium conditions. The dependent outputs are gravitational mass and spin period, reported in solar masses and milliseconds. The frozen formal reasoning plan supplies the candidate propositions and a six-step forward derivation; this section consumes that structure to define the computational protocol without re-listing its unresolved symbols. The derivation begins by applying the relaxation to the static equilibrium constraint, then derives a candidate mass-spin relation, evaluates the mass limit at millisecond periods, checks the causality bound, and finally contrasts the resulting track with isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down. The protocol inherits the status of each step from the formal plan: the first step is proposed and the remaining steps are unverified, so the design is a verification schedule, not an established result.

The design tests the relaxed-axiom mechanism against a declared alternative in which standard stiff equations of state plus rotational support from binary spin-up already account for massive millisecond pulsars without any relaxation of the fundamental nuclear axioms. The comparison is therefore a model-competition protocol: the relaxed-axiom track must produce a mass-spin relation that the standard-support track cannot reproduce within the same causal bound. Ablations isolate each control axis. Removing the rotational and thermal support term collapses the model to the static limit, and tightening the causality bound tests whether the predicted masses survive the speed-of-sound constraint. Robustness is treated as a numerical-implementation problem. The MESA binary module supplies the computational precedent for differentially rotating stars and implicit mass-transfer schemes, but it explicitly excludes common-envelope and contact-binary phases, so those phases are declared out of scope rather than silently absorbed. The Aquila comparison project demonstrates that code-to-code variation in subgrid physics can dominate the result even at fixed initial conditions; the design consequently requires a cross-implementation check before any mass-spin relation is treated as model-independent.

| Condition | Design role | Consequence if violated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Causality bound (c_s <= c) | Hard control on every candidate equation of state | The relaxed axioms are rejected as physically inadmissible |
| Static TOV limit | Reference baseline the relaxation must exceed | No mass-accumulation claim beyond the static maximum |
| Massive MSP population (M > 2.0 M_sun, ms periods) | Empirical consistency target | The predicted mass-spin relation contradicts the observed population |
| Standard rotational support | Declared alternative explanation | The relaxation is unnecessary and the mechanism is not favored |
| Common-envelope / contact phases | Declared out of scope | Results cannot be extended into these regimes |

The taxonomy separates a would-falsify condition from a scope delimiter. Violation of the causality bound or contradiction with the observed massive-millisecond-pulsar population are would-falsify events for the mechanism. The exclusion of common-envelope and contact-binary phases is a scope delimiter: it bounds where the protocol applies and does not, by itself, refute the claim. The standard-support alternative is a competing mechanism that, if it fully reproduces the observations, removes the need for the relaxation.

The verification protocol maps each prespecified outcome branch to an allowed conclusion. A result consistent with the declared relation while the planned controls do not favor the standard-support alternative yields the supports_mechanism branch, which supports but does not prove the relation within the design boundary. Variation across declared conditions, units, or measurement contexts yields partial_or_heterogeneous and forbids a universal conclusion. A comparison that does not support the relation, or that favors the declared alternative, yields null_or_contradictory; absence of support is not proof of absence generally. A failure of quality control, protocol deviation, or validity criterion yields uninformative_or_invalid and warrants no scientific conclusion until the prerequisite is resolved. The counterexample analyzer batch was discarded and is not retained, so no counterexample is claimed; the boundary analysis above is the design-level substitute until qualified human review replaces it. The protocol consumes the formal plan's proof obligations as verification targets rather than treating them as completed proofs.

The MESA infrastructure provides bit-for-bit consistency across supported platforms, and the design adopts that standard as the reproducibility target for the numerical implementation. The measurement plan, quality-control procedure, data-management policy, and reproducibility protocol are not yet finalized and require human input before the design is treated as executable; the measurement plan in particular must specify how gravitational mass and spin period are operationalized, including the method for masses above 2.0 solar masses and the timing procedure for millisecond periods. These four unresolved records are the only human-review dependencies owned by this section, and they gate the transition from the design protocol to the verification stage. The detailed definition ledger and the risk-and-review ledger are owned elsewhere and are referenced here only as the sources of the unresolved symbols and the review gates.

claim_provenance.statement: The theoretical unit of analysis is a static model that relaxes the dense-matter equilibrium axioms to include rotational and thermal support, with mass and spin period as the dependent outputs and the binary accretion parameters, causality bound, and equilibrium conditions as the independent axes.

The comparison protocol tests the relaxed-axiom track against the standard stiff-equation-of-state plus rotational-support alternative, ablates the rotational and thermal support term and the causality bound, and requires a cross-implementation robustness check given documented code-to-code sensitivity.

The boundary taxonomy separates would-falsify conditions (causality violation, contradiction with the observed massive-millisecond-pulsar population) from scope delimiters (excluded common-envelope and contact phases) and from the competing standard-support mechanism.

The decision protocol maps each prespecified outcome branch to its allowed conclusion, and no counterexample is claimed because the counterexample analyzer batch was discarded pending qualified human review.

The measurement plan, quality-control procedure, data-management policy, and reproducibility protocol require human input before the design is executable, with bit-for-bit consistency adopted as the reproducibility target.
